# Chicago Move-Out Prep for a 2-Bedroom Apartment

Your lease ends on **2026-08-31**, so the safest approach is to start planning now and finish with a documented walkthrough, written deposit request, and clean handoff of keys. The goal is to protect your security deposit and leave a clear paper trail.

## Move-Out Checklist and Deposit Email Plan

### Move-Out Checklist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

- **Review your lease now**
  - Confirm notice requirements, cleaning standards, key return rules, and any move-out fees.
- **Give written notice**
  - Send your move-out notice on time and keep a copy.
- **Schedule utilities**
  - Set shutoff or transfer dates for electricity, gas, internet, and water if applicable.
- **Use up supplies**
  - Finish food, discard trash, and remove all personal items from closets, cabinets, balcony, and storage.
- **Clean every room**
  - Wipe appliances, counters, sinks, baseboards, vents, and inside drawers.
  - Vacuum and mop floors; clean bathrooms thoroughly.
- **Patch small damage**
  - Fill tiny nail holes if your lease allows it; do not attempt major repairs without approval.
- **Check fixtures**
  - Replace burnt-out bulbs, test smoke detectors if required, and make sure everything you report is accurate.
- **Return all items**
  - Gather keys, fobs, garage remotes, mailbox keys, parking passes, and access cards.
- **Do a final walkthrough**
  - Compare the apartment to your move-in photos and note anything that remains.
- **Mail forwarding**
  - Set up USPS forwarding and update your address with banks, employer, and subscriptions.

### How to Document Apartment Condition
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/camera.svg

- **Take dated photos and short videos**
  - Capture every room, plus close-ups of floors, walls, appliances, windows, bathrooms, and closets.
- **Use the same angles as your move-in photos**
  - This makes comparison easier if there is a dispute.
- **Photograph existing damage clearly**
  - Include scratches, stains, chips, worn carpet, and any appliance issues.
- **Record meter readings if relevant**
  - Take photos of utility meters or thermostats if you are responsible for them.
- **Save everything in one folder**
  - Name files by room and date, such as `LivingRoom_2026-08-29.jpg`.
- **Request a walkthrough if possible**
  - Ask the landlord or property manager to inspect the unit with you before you leave.
- **Keep proof of delivery**
  - Save emails, texts, and any receipt showing you returned keys and vacated on time.

### Security Deposit Email Sample
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/envelope.svg

Subject: Security Deposit Return Timeline for 2026-08-31 Move-Out

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I hope you are doing well. I’m writing to confirm the move-out process for my apartment and to ask about the timeline for returning my security deposit after I vacate on **2026-08-31**.

Please let me know:
- when the final inspection will take place,
- where and how I should return the keys and access items,
- the expected timeline for the deposit return, and
- whether you need a forwarding address from me in writing.

I plan to leave the apartment clean and return all keys, fobs, and other access items on time. If there are any move-out instructions I should follow, please send them over and I’ll make sure to complete everything.

Thank you for your help.

Best,
[Your Full Name]
[Apartment Address]
[Phone Number]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Download Checklist] https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/articles/renting-apartment-or-house#movingout
Action: [Button: USPS Forwarding] https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm
Action: [Button: Illinois Tenant Help] https://www.illinoislegalaid.org/legal-information/renters-rights-and-responsibilities

## Sources

- Illinois tenant guidance: https://www.illinoislegalaid.org/legal-information/renters-rights-and-responsibilities
- USPS change of address: https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm
- FTC renting and moving out basics: https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/articles/renting-apartment-or-house#movingout
